narration.text: Searchbloom says it publishes this agency list and ranks itself first, making that position its own ranking rather than an independent verdict.
Searchbloom says the facts come from company websites, while case-study figures are the companies’ own reporting.

scenes.visual_direction: Place the self-ranking disclosure and case-study sourcing in two stacked cards, bringing each forward as its narration is heard.

narration.text: For success, Searchbloom recommends leads, sign-ups, or revenue from AI referrals, rather than citation counts or visibility scores.
For evidence, Searchbloom's report recommends requesting a dated AI search result with a named or described company, a figure, and a period.
According to Searchbloom, promises of AI citations in weeks and reports counting citations without mentioning leads or revenue are red flags.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom recommends tracking leads from AI referrals

scenes.visual_direction: Center the outcome takeaway beside an abstract evidence card; reveal empty date, company, figure, and period compartments without adding example results.

narration.text: AI answers are probabilistic: repeating the same question can produce different brands.
Searchbloom's report calls for daily tracking of fixed, real buyer questions across the AI platforms buyers use, then reading the trend.
According to Searchbloom, branded and non-branded prompts should be separated and segmented by awareness, consideration, and purchase.
For measurement details, Searchbloom says to ask which tracking tool, prompts, platforms, and run frequency an agency uses.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom says to track buyer questions daily

scenes.visual_direction: Animate one question card returning different abstract answer arrangements, then organize repeated question cards into a calendar grid without numerical results or trend lines.

narration.text: In Searchbloom’s own tracking, about nine of every ten sources AI cites are on other people’s sites.
To explore those pages, Searchbloom says to request the outside URLs retrieved and cited for top buyer questions, including placements the agency can help secure.
According to Searchbloom, when an answer omits a business, inspecting the cited pages often points to a listing through outreach, a review, or sponsorship.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom says to request outside cited URLs

scenes.visual_direction: Arrange an abstract answer panel beside outside-page cards; draw connectors from the answer to those cards, then highlight one card as the inspection step is discussed.

narration.text: Crawler access, correct structured data, and clean architecture make a site legible to AI platforms.
According to Searchbloom, technical, content, and entity work belongs with the agency, alongside tracking reviewed monthly with the client.
Searchbloom's report recommends clarifying whether the agency builds changes or supplies recommendations, and pricing the developer time the client must provide.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom says to clarify builds versus recommendations

scenes.visual_direction: Arrange a site schematic showing technical work above two lanes for implementation and recommendations; reveal a developer task card in each lane as the narration explains delivery responsibilities.

narration.text: According to Searchbloom, the client must own sponsorship and affiliate budgets when the category's most-retrieved roundup is a paid placement.
Searchbloom says the client's team must also own retailer, marketplace, and partner listings.
Searchbloom's report also places social media and community work, plus brand positioning and the budget behind PR, with the client's team.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom says clients own the PR budget

scenes.visual_direction: Place a client-team silhouette at the center and connect abstract budget, listing, and community cards around it; emphasize the budget card during the closing sentence.

narration.text: Commercial details are not uniformly published: of the nine listed companies, three publish a fee, two a minimum, and four a contract term.
For unpublished fees, minimums, and contract lengths, Searchbloom's report recommends getting the terms in writing before comparing agencies.

on_screen.text: Searchbloom says to get unpublished terms in writing

scenes.visual_direction: Arrange three document compartments for fee, minimum, and contract information, using only abstract marks; consolidate them into one written-terms document as the final takeaway appears.
